summary: Governance is directionally coherent and its codified top priorities still match the product stack, but health remains yellow because the product's main value gaps are still execution gaps: the governance assembly is not yet clearly consumable/verifiable enough, and machine-checkable governance does not yet cover assembly integrity/completeness strongly enough.

topPriorities.title: Operate Governance as a real product with explicit outcomes and reviewable progress
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Governance should model the same explicit goal/evidence/priority discipline it expects from the rest of the portfolio.
topPriorities.currentStatus: Still current. Product intent, plan, metrics, and recent research all reinforce the need to keep Governance operated as a real product rather than letting it dissolve into ambient maintenance.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Continue using explicit priorities, metrics, review outputs, and product-local evidence to assess Governance as a product rather than as background platform hygiene.

topPriorities.title: Complete Governance assembly v0.1 into a clearly consumable and verifiable pack
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Governance only becomes transferable downstream value when the assembly can be installed, verified, reviewed, and maintained without hidden assumptions.
topPriorities.currentStatus: Still current. Risks and interfaces both show the assembly question is still unresolved enough to be an active product concern, not a solved packaging detail.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Make the packaging/consumability decision explicit and keep verification semantics aligned with the chosen packaging model.

topPriorities.title: Extend machine-checkable governance toward the assembly surface and source-of-truth integrity
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Governance gains leverage from validation, so the next control-quality gain is reducing drift between product state, assembly state, and shipped repo state.
topPriorities.currentStatus: Still current. The plan, risks, metrics, interfaces, and implementation memo all point to assembly integrity/completeness as the next meaningful machine-checkable extension.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Define and stage the next validation path for assembly integrity/completeness and preserve explicit linkage across product, assembly, and source-of-truth surfaces.

blockers.title: Governance assembly consumability decision remains under-specified
blockers.impact: Prevents Governance from being clearly portable and reviewable as a downstream-consumable pack.

blockers.title: Machine-checkable governance coverage does not yet fully include assembly integrity/completeness
blockers.impact: Leaves a gap between governance intent and enforceable control over what the assembly actually exports.

risks.title: Governance product can lag behind the standards it expects from other products
Governance assembly remains scaffolded rather than truly consumable
Machine-checkable governance does not yet cover the governance assembly surface strongly enough
Registry and source-of-truth relationships can drift

proposedTdeActions.title: Confirm Governance assembly v0.1 packaging/consumability decision
proposedTdeActions.why: This is the clearest bottleneck to making Governance portable, reviewable, and verifiable downstream.

proposedTdeActions.title: Define the next validator/control increment for assembly integrity/completeness
proposedTdeActions.why: This closes the main leverage gap between Governance policy intent and machine-checkable enforcement.

proposedTdeActions.title: Maintain explicit product-local review discipline for Governance
proposedTdeActions.why: Governance credibility depends on visibly applying the same explicit priority/metrics/review standard it requires elsewhere.
